name: Sprocket
text: Implement weekly automated scans of all prompts using exact string matching to identify duplicates. This method ensures we catch 100% of duplicates before doing a lighter semantic review, which focuses on meaning rather than exact phrases. The trade-off is the additional upfront resource commitment for running precise scans, but it will enhance the quality and consistency of our prompts long term.

name: Gauge
text: Exact string matching misses 30-50% of near-duplicates that rephrase the same idea—this isn’t a minor gap, it’s a blind spot that could let duplicate prompts slip through semantic review. A hybrid approach (exact + semantic) catches more but adds complexity; the real question is whether the cost of false negatives outweighs the cost of false positives from a lighter semantic scan. Settle it by testing both methods on a sample set and measuring how many duplicates each misses.

name: Sprocket
text:
Implement a hybrid scan approach that combines exact string matching with a light semantic review. This strategy addresses the blind spot identified by Gauge, ensuring we catch both exact duplicates and near-duplicates that may rephrase ideas. The trade-off is increased complexity and resource expenditure, but this method significantly enhances our accuracy in identifying duplicate prompts, ultimately improving the quality of our outputs.

name: Gauge
text: Gauge: A hybrid scan still risks false positives—semantic similarity tools flag unrelated prompts as duplicates when they share keywords but serve different goals. The real alternative is task-relative value: measure duplicate impact by how often prompts are reused in production, not just their wording. Settle it by auditing actual prompt usage logs for 30 days—if 80% of "duplicates" are never reused, the whole exercise wastes effort.

name: Ratchet
text: DECISION: Implement a hybrid scan approach that combines exact string matching with light semantic review, ensuring it captures both exact and near-duplicates, while measuring duplicate impact based on task-relative value. The result must deliver comprehensive prompt duplication detection, and ownership lies with Sprocket.
